description: Delney, Streetwise Lookout + Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy + a 1-mana nonland source (Devoted Druid): Kinnan's own 'whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana' trigger is itself a power-2-or-less creature's triggered ability, so Delney causes it to trigger an additional time — one tap yields +2 mana on top of the source's own output (here, 1 + 2 = 3, which happens to triple a 1-mana source specifically; see GBS-0003 for a 2-mana source, where it is 2 + 2 = 4, not a triple). Validates INT-0013.
artificial_state_elements: Devoted Druid was chosen as the tapped nonland mana source purely because it is already a proven, in-repo fixture from GBS-0001/INT-0002 and produces a single, unambiguous mana type ({G}) with no choice required — its specific identity is not material to the rule under test (Delney doubling Kinnan's own trigger); any nonland mana-producing permanent would exercise the same rule.
No other permanents, hand cards, lands, or players' boards were modeled — this is a three-card isolation test, not a representative game state.
Only a single mana activation was performed (not a full turn's worth of mana development) since the rule being tested applies identically and independently to each individual tap.
material_characteristics: Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy's power is exactly 2, so its own triggered mana ability qualifies for Delney's power-2-or-less doubling clause

Kinnan's 'Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana of any type that permanent produced' ability is itself a triggered ability (word 'Whenever'), and specifically a triggered mana ability under CR 605.1b

Delney's static ability causes any triggered ability of a creature it controls with power 2 or less to trigger an additional time (CR 603.2d), including Kinnan's own trigger, without requiring a third card
The mana source tapped must be a nonland permanent (Kinnan's trigger condition explicitly excludes lands)
abstracted_characteristics: Identity of the specific nonland mana source tapped (any would trigger Kinnan/Delney identically)
All board state not directly involved in the three-card interaction
Turn/phase beyond what's needed to activate one mana ability in a single main phase

legal_actions: Activate Devoted Druid's mana ability ({T}: Add {G})
illegal_actions_to_reject: Any implicit assumption that tapping the nonland mana source only nets double mana (Kinnan alone) rather than +2 on top of the source's own output (Kinnan's trigger plus Delney's extra copy of that same trigger)
Generalizing this specific 1-mana-source result ('triple') into 'Delney+Kinnan triples all nonland mana sources' — it does not; see GBS-0003 for the 2-mana counterexample (2 -> 4, not 6)
expected.outcome_if_resolved: After activating Devoted Druid's mana ability once: 3 total {G} in the player's mana pool (1 original + 1 from Kinnan's own trigger + 1 from Delney doubling that trigger), and Devoted Druid tapped. This is Devoted Druid's own 1 mana plus a flat +2, which for a 1-mana source happens to equal a triple.

rules_citations: CR 603.2d (a triggered ability may be stated to trigger an additional time; determine how many times, then trigger that many times)

CR 605.1b (a triggered ability that doesn't require a target, triggers from activation/resolution of an activated mana ability or from mana being added to a pool, and could add mana to a pool when it resolves, is itself a triggered mana ability)

CR 605.4 / 605.4a (triggered mana abilities follow all the rules for other triggered abilities including 603.2d, but do not use the stack and resolve immediately after the mana ability that triggered them)
